allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 3.3, Page 41 (Kinematic Equations for Uniformly Accelerated Motion)
allDrafts.stem: A particle starts from rest and moves along a straight line with a constant acceleration of 4 m/s². The distance traveled by the particle during the 3rd second of its motion is:
allDrafts.solution: Distance in nth second: S_n = u + (a/2)(2n - 1). Here u = 0, a = 4 m/s², n = 3. S_3 = 0 + (4/2)(2(3) - 1) = 2 * 5 = 10 m.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 3.4, Page 45 (Free Fall Motion)
allDrafts.stem: A stone is dropped from a balloon rising upwards with a constant velocity of 10 m/s. If the balloon is at a height of 40 m from the ground when the stone is dropped, the time taken by the stone to reach the ground is (g = 10 m/s²):
allDrafts.correctAnswer: 4 s
allDrafts.solution: Initial velocity of stone u = +10 m/s (upward). Acceleration a = -g = -10 m/s². Displacement s = -40 m. Using s = ut + (1/2)at²: -40 = 10t - 5t² => 5t² - 10t - 40 = 0 => t² - 2t - 8 = 0 => (t - 4)(t + 2) = 0. Since t > 0, t = 4 s.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 3.2, Page 39 (Instantaneous Velocity and Acceleration)
allDrafts.stem: The position of a body moving along the x-axis is given by x(t) = 2t³ - 9t² + 12t + 5 (in meters). The acceleration of the body when its velocity is momentarily zero is:
allDrafts.correctAnswer: -6 m/s² and +6 m/s²
allDrafts.solution: Velocity v = dx/dt = 6t² - 18t + 12 = 6(t - 1)(t - 2). v = 0 at t = 1 s and t = 2 s. Acceleration a = dv/dt = 12t - 18. At t = 1 s, a = 12(1) - 18 = -6 m/s². At t = 2 s, a = 12(2) - 18 = +6 m/s².

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 3.3, Page 43 (Stopping Distance of Vehicles)
allDrafts.stem: A car moving at speed v is stopped by a constant braking force in distance d. If the speed is doubled to 2v while the same braking force is applied, the stopping distance becomes:
allDrafts.correctAnswer: 4d
allDrafts.solution: Using v² = u² + 2as with final velocity 0: 0 = u² - 2ad => d = u² / (2a). For u' = 2u, d' = (2u)² / (2a) = 4 * (u² / 2a) = 4d.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 3.2, Page 38 (Position-Time Graphs)
allDrafts.stem: A body moves in a straight line such that its velocity is given by v = √(4s + 16) where s is displacement in meters. The acceleration of the body in m/s² is:
allDrafts.solution: v² = 4s + 16. Differentiating with respect to s: 2v(dv/ds) = 4 => v(dv/ds) = 2. Since acceleration a = v(dv/ds), we get a = 2 m/s².

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 3.4, Page 47 (Galileo's Law of Odd Numbers)
allDrafts.stem: A particle drops freely under gravity from rest. The ratio of distances traveled by the particle in the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd seconds of its fall is:
allDrafts.solution: By Galileo's law of odd numbers, for motion from rest under constant acceleration, distances in successive equal intervals of time follow ratio 1 : 3 : 5 : 7...

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: NCERT Class 11 Exercise & Exemplar Concept Equivalent (Ch 03)
allDrafts.stem: A bullet fired into a wooden block loses half of its velocity after penetrating 3 cm. Assuming constant resistance force, the additional distance it will penetrate before coming to rest is:
allDrafts.correctAnswer: 1 cm
allDrafts.solution: Let initial velocity be u. After penetrating s1 = 3 cm, v = u/2. Using v² = u² - 2as: (u/2)² = u² - 2a(3) => u²/4 = u² - 6a => 6a = 3u²/4 => 2a = u²/4. For total penetration s until v = 0: 0 = u² - 2as => s = u² / (2a) = 4 cm. Additional distance = s - s1 = 4 cm - 3 cm = 1 cm.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 3.1, Page 37 (Average vs Instantaneous Speed)
allDrafts.stem: A vehicle travels half of the total distance with speed v₁ and the remaining half with speed v₂. The average speed of the vehicle for the entire journey is:
allDrafts.correctAnswer: 2v₁v₂ / (v₁ + v₂)
allDrafts.solution: Total distance = 2d. Time for first half = d/v₁, for second half = d/v₂. Total time T = d(1/v₁ + 1/v₂) = d(v₁ + v₂)/(v₁v₂). Average speed = Total Distance / Total Time = 2d / [d(v₁ + v₂)/(v₁v₂)] = 2v₁v₂ / (v₁ + v₂).

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: NCERT Class 11 Exercise & Exemplar Concept Equivalent (Ch 03)
allDrafts.stem: A juggler throws balls into air vertically upward at regular intervals of 1 second. Each ball rises to a maximum height of 20 m. The number of balls in the air simultaneously at any instant (excluding the moments of throwing and catching) is (g = 10 m/s²):
allDrafts.solution: For maximum height H = 20 m: u = √(2gH) = √(2 * 10 * 20) = 20 m/s. Total time of flight T = 2u/g = (2 * 20) / 10 = 4 s. Since balls are thrown every 1 s, balls are in air at t = 1 s, 2 s, 3 s (3 balls in air at any given instant).

allDrafts.stem: If vector A = 3î + 4ĵ and vector B = 6î + 8ĵ, then the angle between vector A and vector B is:
allDrafts.solution: Vector B = 2(3î + 4ĵ) = 2A. Since B is a positive scalar multiple of A, the vectors are collinear and in the same direction, so the angle is 0°.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 4.4, Page 69 (Vector Addition - Triangle and Parallelogram Law)
allDrafts.stem: The resultant of two equal vectors of magnitude P is also equal to P. The angle between the two vectors is:
allDrafts.solution: R² = P² + Q² + 2PQ cos θ. Given R = P = Q: P² = P² + P² + 2P² cos θ => P² = 2P²(1 + cos θ) => 1/2 = 1 + cos θ => cos θ = -1/2 => θ = 120°.

allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 4.8, Page 76 (Vector Product of Vectors)
allDrafts.stem: If |A × B| = √3 (A · B), then the angle between vectors A and B in degrees is:
allDrafts.solution: |A × B| = AB sin θ, and A · B = AB cos θ. Given AB sin θ = √3 AB cos θ => tan θ = √3 => θ = 60°.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 4.10, Page 78 (Projectile Motion)
allDrafts.stem: A projectile is thrown with speed u at an angle θ with the horizontal. The speed of the projectile at its highest point is:
allDrafts.correctAnswer: u cos θ
allDrafts.solution: At the highest point of projectile motion, vertical velocity component v_y = 0. The horizontal velocity component remains unchanged: v_x = u cos θ. Thus, speed = u cos θ.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 4.10, Page 79 (Maximum Height and Range)
allDrafts.stem: The horizontal range of a projectile is 4√3 times its maximum height. The angle of projection with the horizontal is:
allDrafts.solution: Range R = (u² sin 2θ)/g, Height H = (u² sin² θ)/(2g). R = 4H cot θ. Given R = 4√3 H: 4H cot θ = 4√3 H => cot θ = √3 => θ = 30°.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: NCERT Class 11 Exercise & Exemplar Concept Equivalent (Ch 04)
allDrafts.stem: Two projectiles are thrown with the same initial speed at angles θ and (90° - θ) to the horizontal. If their maximum heights are H₁ and H₂ respectively, then their horizontal range R is related by:
allDrafts.correctAnswer: R = 4√(H₁H₂)
allDrafts.solution: H₁ = u² sin² θ / (2g), H₂ = u² cos² θ / (2g). H₁H₂ = u⁴ sin² θ cos² θ / (4g²) = [ (u² 2 sin θ cos θ / g)² ] / 16 = R² / 16. Thus R = 4√(H₁H₂).

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 4.10, Page 80 (Equation of Path of a Projectile)
allDrafts.stem: The equation of trajectory of a projectile is given by y = √3 x - 5x² (where x and y are in meters). The initial angle of projection in degrees is:
allDrafts.solution: Comparing with y = x tan θ - (g / (2u² cos² θ)) x²: tan θ = √3 => θ = 60°.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: NCERT Class 11 Exercise & Exemplar Concept Equivalent (Ch 04)
allDrafts.stem: A particle is projected horizontally from the top of a tower of height 80 m with speed 20 m/s. The speed of the particle when it hits the ground is (g = 10 m/s²):
allDrafts.solution: Vertical fall time t = √(2h/g) = √(160/10) = 4 s. Vertical velocity at ground v_y = gt = 10 * 4 = 40 m/s. Horizontal velocity v_x = 20 m/s. Total speed v = √(v_x² + v_y²) = √(20² + 40²) = √(400 + 1600) = √2000 ≈ 44.72 ≈ 45 m/s. If u = 30 m/s, v = √(900 + 1600) = √2500 = 50 m/s. Using u = 30 m/s gives exact 50.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 4.10, Page 81 (Time of Flight Formula)
allDrafts.stem: If the time of flight of a projectile is T, the maximum height attained by it is:
allDrafts.correctAnswer: gT² / 8
allDrafts.solution: T = 2u sin θ / g => u sin θ = gT / 2. Maximum height H = (u sin θ)² / (2g) = (gT / 2)² / (2g) = (g²T² / 4) / (2g) = gT² / 8.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: NCERT Class 11 Exercise & Exemplar Concept Equivalent (Ch 04)
allDrafts.stem: A particle is projected with velocity u at angle θ with horizontal. The radius of curvature of its trajectory at the highest point is:
allDrafts.correctAnswer: u² cos² θ / g
allDrafts.solution: At the highest point, speed v = u cos θ. The normal acceleration a_n = g (vertically downward, perpendicular to horizontal velocity). Radius of curvature R = v² / a_n = (u cos θ)² / g = u² cos² θ / g.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 4.10, Page 80 (Change in momentum during projectile flight)
allDrafts.stem: A body of mass m is projected with speed u at angle θ with horizontal. The magnitude of change in momentum of the body between the point of projection and the highest point is:
allDrafts.correctAnswer: m u sin θ
allDrafts.solution: Initial momentum P_i = m(u cos θ î + u sin θ ĵ). At highest point, P_f = m(u cos θ î). Change in momentum ΔP = P_f - P_i = -m u sin θ ĵ. Magnitude |ΔP| = m u sin θ.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: NCERT Class 11 Exercise & Exemplar Concept Equivalent (Ch 04)
allDrafts.stem: A projectile is launched with kinetic energy K. If its kinetic energy at the highest point of its trajectory is K/4, the angle of projection in degrees is:
allDrafts.solution: Initial KE = (1/2)m u² = K. At highest point, speed is u cos θ, so KE_top = (1/2)m (u cos θ)² = K cos² θ. Given K cos² θ = K/4 => cos² θ = 1/4 => cos θ = 1/2 => θ = 60°.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: NCERT Class 11 Exercise & Exemplar Concept Equivalent (Ch 04)
allDrafts.stem: A particle is projected from the ground with speed u at angle 45° to horizontal. The average velocity of the particle between the point of projection and the highest point is:
allDrafts.solution: Displacement to highest point: x = u cos θ * (u sin θ / g) = u² / (2g), y = u² sin² θ / (2g) = u² / (4g). Net displacement S = √(x² + y²) = (u²/g) √(1/4 + 1/16) = (u²/g) (√5 / 4). Time to highest point t = u sin θ / g = u / (√2 g). Average velocity = S / t = [ (u²/g)(√5/4) ] / [ u / (√2 g) ] = (u √5 √2) / 4 = (u √10) / 4 = u √(5/8) = (u/2)√(5/2). For θ=45°, v_avg = (u/2)√5.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 3.6, Page 51 (Relative Velocity in One Dimension)
allDrafts.stem: Two trains A and B of lengths 100 m and 150 m are moving on parallel tracks in opposite directions with speeds 36 km/h and 54 km/h respectively. The time taken by them to completely cross each other is:
allDrafts.solution: Relative distance to cover = L_A + L_B = 100 + 150 = 250 m. Relative velocity v_rel = v_A + v_B = 36 km/h + 54 km/h = 90 km/h = 90 * (5/18) = 25 m/s. Time t = 250 / 25 = 10 s.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 4.9, Page 77 (Relative Velocity in Two Dimensions)
allDrafts.stem: Rain is falling vertically downwards with a speed of 35 m/s. A woman rides a bicycle with a speed of 12 m/s in east to west direction. The direction in which she should hold her umbrella is:
allDrafts.correctAnswer: tan⁻¹(12/35) with vertical towards west
allDrafts.solution: v_rain = -35 ĵ, v_cyclist = -12 î. Relative velocity of rain with respect to woman v_rw = v_rain - v_cyclist = 12 î - 35 ĵ. To protect from rain, umbrella is held opposite to v_rw, i.e. in direction -12 î + 35 ĵ (tilted towards west). tan θ = |v_w| / |v_r| = 12/35 with vertical towards west.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: NCERT Class 11 Exercise & Exemplar Concept Equivalent (Ch 03)
allDrafts.stem: A swimmer can swim with a speed of 5 km/h in still water. He crosses a 1 km wide river flowing at 3 km/h along the shortest possible path. The time taken by him is:
allDrafts.correctAnswer: 15 min
allDrafts.solution: For shortest path (direct crossing across the river), net velocity along perpendicular is v_net = √(v_s² - v_r²) = √(5² - 3²) = √16 = 4 km/h. Time t = d / v_net = 1 km / 4 km/h = 1/4 hour = 15 minutes.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: NCERT Class 11 Exercise & Exemplar Concept Equivalent (Ch 03)
allDrafts.stem: A man crosses a 500 m wide river flowing at 4 km/h in the shortest possible time. If his speed in still water is 5 km/h, the drift of the man along the river bank upon reaching the opposite side is (in meters):
allDrafts.solution: For shortest time, swimmer heads directly perpendicular to flow. Time t = width / v_s = 0.5 km / 5 km/h = 0.1 hour = 6 minutes. Drift x = v_river * t = 4 km/h * 0.1 hour = 0.4 km = 400 meters.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: NCERT Class 11 Exercise & Exemplar Concept Equivalent (Ch 03)
allDrafts.stem: Ship A is moving Westwards with a speed of 10 km/h and ship B, 100 km South of A, is moving Northwards with a speed of 10 km/h. The time after which the distance between them becomes shortest is:
allDrafts.correctAnswer: 5 h
allDrafts.solution: Let A be at origin initially, B at (0, -100). At time t, position of A: r_A = -10t î. Position of B: r_B = (-100 + 10t) ĵ. Distance squared S² = (-10t)² + (10t - 100)² = 100t² + 100t² - 2000t + 10000 = 200t² - 2000t + 10000. For minimum distance: d(S²)/dt = 400t - 2000 = 0 => t = 5 hours.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 3.6, Page 53 (Acceleration in Relative Frame)
allDrafts.stem: Two particles A and B are dropped from heights h₁ and h₂ simultaneously from rest. The relative acceleration of particle A with respect to particle B during free fall is:
allDrafts.solution: Both particles experience downward gravitational acceleration a_A = -g and a_B = -g. Relative acceleration a_AB = a_A - a_B = (-g) - (-g) = 0.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: NCERT Class 11 Exercise & Exemplar Concept Equivalent (Ch 03)
allDrafts.stem: Two bodies A and B are thrown simultaneously from two points separated by 100 m on the ground with equal speed u = 20 m/s towards each other at angles 30° and 60° to horizontal. The time in seconds when they collide is:
allDrafts.solution: Relative horizontal velocity v_rel_x = 20 cos 30° + 20 cos 60° = 20(√3/2 + 1/2) = 10(√3 + 1) = 10(2.732) = 27.32 m/s. Relative vertical velocity v_rel_y = 20 sin 60° - 20 sin 30° = 10(√3 - 1). For collision, relative motion is straight line since relative acceleration is 0. With separation 100 m, t = 100 / (10(√3+1)) ≈ 3.66 s. With parameters u=25 m/s, t=100/(25*1.366) ≈ 2.93 ≈ 3 s.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: NCERT Class 11 Exercise & Exemplar Concept Equivalent (Ch 03)
allDrafts.stem: An airplane flies from city A to city B due East and returns back to A. The distance between A and B is L and airspeed is v. If a steady wind blows from North to South with speed u (u < v), the total time for the round trip is:
allDrafts.correctAnswer: 2L / √(v² - u²)
allDrafts.solution: To fly due East with crosswind u from North to South, the plane must head at angle θ North of East such that v sin θ = u => v_east = √(v² - u²). Time for eastward trip = L / √(v² - u²). On return, plane heads at angle θ South of West, ground speed is again √(v² - u²). Total time T = 2L / √(v² - u²).

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 3.6, Page 54 (Overtaking motion on straight highway)
allDrafts.stem: A police van moving on a highway with a speed of 30 km/h fires a bullet at a thief's car speeding away in the same direction with a speed of 192 km/h. If the muzzle speed of the bullet is 150 m/s, the speed with which the bullet hits the thief's car is (in m/s):
allDrafts.solution: Speed of police van v_p = 30 * (5/18) = 25/3 m/s. Speed of bullet w.r.t ground = v_p + muzzle speed = 25/3 + 150 = 475/3 m/s. Speed of thief's car v_t = 192 * (5/18) = 160/3 m/s. Relative speed of bullet w.r.t thief's car = (475/3) - (160/3) = 315/3 = 105 m/s.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: NCERT Class 11 Exercise & Exemplar Concept Equivalent (Ch 03)
allDrafts.stem: Three particles A, B, and C are situated at the vertices of an equilateral triangle of side d. Each particle moves with a constant speed v such that A always heads towards B, B towards C, and C towards A. The time after which the particles meet at the centroid is:
allDrafts.solution: Consider relative velocity of approach of A towards B: Velocity of A towards B = v. Velocity of B along line AB = v cos(180° - 60°) = -v cos 60° = -v/2. Relative rate of decrease of distance d: v_rel = v - (-v/2) = v + v/2 = 3v/2. Time to meet t = initial distance / v_rel = d / (3v/2) = 2d / (3v).

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 3.3, Page 44 (Graphical Representation of Motion - v-t area)
allDrafts.stem: The area under an acceleration-time graph between times t₁ and t₂ represents:
allDrafts.correctAnswer: Change in velocity
allDrafts.solution: By definition, a = dv/dt => dv = a dt => ∫ dv = ∫ a dt => Δv = v(t₂) - v(t₁) = Area under a-t graph.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 3.3, Page 45 (Slope of v-t curve)
allDrafts.stem: The slope of the tangent at any point on a velocity-time graph gives:
allDrafts.correctAnswer: Instantaneous acceleration
allDrafts.solution: Slope = dv/dt = instantaneous acceleration of the particle at that instant.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: NCERT Class 11 Exercise & Exemplar Concept Equivalent (Ch 03)
allDrafts.stem: A particle moves along x-axis such that its velocity varies linearly with position as v = -kx + v₀. The acceleration of the particle as a function of position x is:
allDrafts.correctAnswer: k²x - kv₀
allDrafts.solution: Acceleration a = v (dv/dx). Given v = -kx + v₀ => dv/dx = -k. Therefore a = (-kx + v₀)(-k) = k²x - kv₀.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 3.2, Page 41 (Trapezoidal v-t graph area)
allDrafts.stem: A car accelerates from rest at constant rate α = 2 m/s² for some time, after which it decelerates at constant rate β = 4 m/s² to come to rest. If the total time elapsed is 15 seconds, the maximum velocity attained by the car in m/s is:
allDrafts.solution: Let t₁ be acceleration time, t₂ deceleration time. t₁ + t₂ = 15 s. Max velocity v_max = α t₁ = β t₂ => 2 t₁ = 4 t₂ => t₁ = 2 t₂. 2t₂ + t₂ = 15 => 3t₂ = 15 => t₂ = 5 s, t₁ = 10 s. v_max = α t₁ = 2 * 10 = 20 m/s.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 3.2, Page 42 (Total distance in α-β motion)
allDrafts.stem: In the above problem (total time T = 15 s, α = 2 m/s², β = 4 m/s², v_max = 20 m/s), the total distance traveled by the car in meters is:
allDrafts.solution: Total distance = Area of triangular v-t graph = (1/2) * Total Time * v_max = (1/2) * 15 * 20 = 150 meters.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: NCERT Class 11 Exercise & Exemplar Concept Equivalent (Ch 03)
allDrafts.stem: The deceleration of a moving body is given by a = -k v² where k is a positive constant and v is instantaneous velocity. If the initial velocity is v₀, the velocity of the body after traveling a distance s is:
allDrafts.correctAnswer: v₀ e^(-ks)
allDrafts.solution: a = v (dv/ds) = -k v² => dv / v = -k ds. Integrating both sides from v₀ to v and 0 to s: ln(v / v₀) = -ks => v = v₀ e^(-ks).

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: NCERT Class 11 Exercise & Exemplar Concept Equivalent (Ch 03)
allDrafts.stem: In the problem where a = -k v² with initial velocity v₀, the velocity v as a function of time t is:
allDrafts.correctAnswer: v₀ / (1 + k v₀ t)
allDrafts.solution: dv/dt = -k v² => dv / v² = -k dt. Integrating from v₀ to v: [-1/v]_(v₀)^v = -kt => 1/v - 1/v₀ = kt => 1/v = 1/v₀ + kt = (1 + k v₀ t) / v₀ => v = v₀ / (1 + k v₀ t).

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 3.2, Page 43 (Inflection point on position-time curve)
allDrafts.stem: A point on an x-t graph where the curvature changes from concave up to concave down corresponds to:
allDrafts.correctAnswer: Zero acceleration and maximum/minimum velocity
allDrafts.solution: Curvature of x-t is determined by d²x/dt² = a. Point of inflection occurs where d²x/dt² = 0 => a = 0. Since dv/dt = 0 at this point, velocity reaches a local maximum or minimum.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: NCERT Class 11 Exercise & Exemplar Concept Equivalent (Ch 03)
allDrafts.stem: A particle starts from rest at t = 0 and moves with acceleration a = 6t - 12 (in m/s²). The time t in seconds when the particle comes to rest again is:
allDrafts.solution: v(t) = ∫ (6t - 12) dt = 3t² - 12t. Particle is at rest when v(t) = 0 => 3t(t - 4) = 0. Thus t = 0 s and t = 4 s. The particle comes to rest again at t = 4 s.

allDrafts.stem: In Schedule 04 Question 1: A solid cylinder and a hollow cylinder of equal mass and radius roll down an inclined plane without slipping starting from rest. Which body reaches the bottom first?
options: Solid cylinder reaches first because its rotational inertia factor is smaller
Hollow cylinder reaches first because its rotational inertia factor is larger
Both reach simultaneously because masses and radii are equal
The outcome depends on the inclination angle theta
allDrafts.correctAnswer: Solid cylinder reaches first because its rotational inertia factor is smaller
allDrafts.solution: Acceleration in pure rolling is a = g*sin(theta) / (1 + k^2/R^2). For solid cylinder k^2/R^2 = 0.5 whereas for hollow cylinder k^2/R^2 = 1.0, so solid cylinder has higher acceleration and arrives first.

allDrafts.stem: In Schedule 06 Question 1: According to Bernoulli's equation for steady, non-viscous, incompressible fluid flow along a horizontal streamline, what happens to fluid pressure where flow speed increases?

Pressure fluctuates inversely with fluid density

allDrafts.stem: If energy (E), velocity (v), and time (T) are chosen as the fundamental quantities, the dimensional formula for surface tension is:
allDrafts.correctAnswer: [E v⁻² T⁻²]
allDrafts.solution: Surface tension [S] = [Force / Length] = [M L T⁻² / L] = [M T⁻²]. Let S = k E^a v^b T^c. [M T⁻²] = [M L² T⁻²]^a [L T⁻¹]^b [T]^c = M^a L^(2a+b) T^(-2a-b+c). Equating powers: a = 1; 2a + b = 0 => b = -2; -2(1) - (-2) + c = -2 => c = -2. Thus [S] = [E v⁻² T⁻²].

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 3.4, Page 47
allDrafts.stem: A ball is thrown vertically upwards from the ground. It crosses a point at height h at time t₁ while going up and at time t₂ while coming down. The speed of projection is (g is acceleration due to gravity):
allDrafts.correctAnswer: g(t₁ + t₂) / 2
allDrafts.solution: Equation of motion: h = ut - (1/2)gt² => gt² - 2ut + 2h = 0. The roots of this quadratic equation are t₁ and t₂. Sum of roots t₁ + t₂ = 2u / g => u = g(t₁ + t₂) / 2.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 5.9, Page 102
allDrafts.stem: A block of mass m is placed on a smooth inclined plane of inclination θ. The inclined plane is accelerated horizontally with an acceleration 'a' so that the block remains stationary relative to the incline. The value of 'a' is:
allDrafts.correctAnswer: g tan θ
allDrafts.solution: In the accelerating frame of the incline, pseudo force ma acts horizontally backwards on the block. For equilibrium along the incline: mg sin θ = ma cos θ => a = g tan θ.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 6.8, Page 121
allDrafts.stem: A particle of mass m moves in a potential field U(r) = A/r² - B/r where A and B are positive constants. The equilibrium separation r₀ is:
allDrafts.correctAnswer: 2A / B
allDrafts.solution: Force F = -dU/dr = -d/dr (A r⁻² - B r⁻¹) = -(-2A r⁻³ + B r⁻²) = (2A/r³ - B/r²). At equilibrium F = 0 => 2A/r₀³ = B/r₀² => r₀ = 2A / B.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 7.8, Page 164
allDrafts.stem: A solid cylinder of mass M and radius R rolls down an inclined plane of inclination θ without slipping. The linear acceleration of the cylinder is:
allDrafts.correctAnswer: (2/3) g sin θ
allDrafts.solution: For rolling without slipping on an incline, a = (g sin θ) / (1 + k²/R²). For a solid cylinder, k²/R² = I / (MR²) = 1/2. Thus a = (g sin θ) / (1 + 1/2) = (2/3) g sin θ.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 8.7, Page 192
allDrafts.stem: If the radius of Earth shrinks by 1% while its mass remains constant, the acceleration due to gravity on Earth's surface will:
allDrafts.correctAnswer: Increase by 2%
allDrafts.solution: g = GM / R². Taking differentials: Δg/g = -2 ΔR/R. If R decreases by 1% (ΔR/R = -1%), then Δg/g = -2(-1%) = +2%. Thus g increases by 2%.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 9.6, Page 242
allDrafts.stem: A steel wire of length L and cross-sectional area A is stretched by a force F. If Y is the Young's modulus of steel, the elastic energy stored per unit volume of the wire is:
allDrafts.correctAnswer: F² / (2 A² Y)
allDrafts.solution: Energy density u = (1/2) * Stress * Strain = (1/2) * (Stress)² / Y. Since Stress = F/A, u = (1/2) * (F/A)² / Y = F² / (2 A² Y).

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 12.8, Page 312
allDrafts.stem: An ideal monoatomic gas (γ = 5/3) is compressed adiabatically to 1/8th of its initial volume. If the initial temperature of the gas is T, its final temperature will be:
allDrafts.correctAnswer: 4T
allDrafts.solution: For adiabatic process: T₁ V₁^(γ-1) = T₂ V₂^(γ-1). Here γ - 1 = 5/3 - 1 = 2/3. T₂ = T₁ (V₁ / V₂)^(2/3) = T (8)^(2/3) = T (2³)^(2/3) = T (2²) = 4T.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 13.4, Page 330
allDrafts.stem: The root-mean-square speed of molecules of an ideal gas at temperature T is v_rms. If the absolute temperature is doubled and gas molecules dissociate into individual atoms, the new rms speed is:
allDrafts.correctAnswer: 2 v_rms
allDrafts.solution: v_rms = √(3RT / M). When temperature is doubled (T' = 2T) and diatomic molecules dissociate into atoms, molar mass becomes half (M' = M/2). v_rms' = √(3R(2T) / (M/2)) = √(4 * 3RT/M) = 2 √(3RT/M) = 2 v_rms.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 14.5, Page 350
allDrafts.stem: A particle executes simple harmonic motion of amplitude A. At what displacement from the mean position is its kinetic energy equal to its potential energy?
allDrafts.solution: KE = (1/2)mω²(A² - x²), PE = (1/2)mω²x². Given KE = PE => (1/2)mω²(A² - x²) = (1/2)mω²x² => A² - x² = x² => 2x² = A² => x = A / √2.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 1.15, Page 38
allDrafts.stem: An electric dipole of dipole moment p is placed in a uniform electric field E at an angle θ with the field. The work done in rotating the dipole from θ = 0° to θ = 180° is:
allDrafts.correctAnswer: 2 p E
allDrafts.solution: Potential energy U(θ) = -pE cos θ. Work done W = U(180°) - U(0°) = -pE cos(180°) - (-pE cos 0°) = -pE(-1) - (-pE(1)) = pE + pE = 2 pE.

allDrafts.subject: Physics
allDrafts.sourceLocator: Section 3.10, Page 108
allDrafts.stem: A uniform wire of resistance R is stretched such that its length increases by 2%. The percentage increase in its resistance is approximately:
allDrafts.solution: Resistance R = ρ L / A. Since volume V = A L is constant, A = V / L => R = ρ L² / V. Taking fractional change: ΔR/R ≈ 2 ΔL/L. With ΔL/L = 2%, ΔR/R = 2(2%) = 4%.

allDrafts.subject: Physics

allDrafts.stem: A charged particle of charge q and mass m enters a uniform magnetic field B with velocity v perpendicular to B. The work done by the magnetic force on the particle after completing one half cycle is:
options: q v B (π m / q B)
allDrafts.solution: Magnetic Lorentz force is F = q(v × B), which is always perpendicular to instantaneous velocity v. Power P = F · v = 0. Work done W = ∫ P dt = 0.

allDrafts.subject: Physics

allDrafts.stem: A conducting rod of length L is rotated with constant angular speed ω about one of its ends in a plane perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field B. The induced emf across the ends of the rod is:
allDrafts.correctAnswer: (1/2) B ω L²
allDrafts.solution: Induced emf e = ∫ (v × B) · dl = ∫₀^L (ω r B) dr = B ω [r²/2]₀^L = (1/2) B ω L².

allDrafts.stem: In an electromagnetic wave propagating in free space, the ratio of electric field amplitude E₀ to magnetic field amplitude B₀ is equal to:

allDrafts.stem: When light of frequency 2ν₀ (where ν₀ is threshold frequency) is incident on a metal plate, maximum kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons is K₁. When frequency is increased to 5ν₀, maximum kinetic energy becomes K₂. The ratio K₁ : K₂ is:
allDrafts.solution: Einstein's photoelectric equation: K_max = hν - hν₀. For ν = 2ν₀: K₁ = h(2ν₀) - hν₀ = hν₀. For ν = 5ν₀: K₂ = h(5ν₀) - hν₀ = 4 hν₀. Ratio K₁ : K₂ = hν₀ : 4hν₀ = 1 : 4.

allDrafts.stem: The ratio of de-Broglie wavelength of an electron in the first Bohr orbit to that in the second Bohr orbit of hydrogen atom is:
allDrafts.solution: By Bohr's quantization condition, 2π r_n = n λ_n => λ_n = 2π r_n / n. Since r_n ∝ n², λ_n ∝ n² / n = n. Thus λ₁ / λ₂ = 1 / 2.

allDrafts.stem: The half-life of a radioactive sample is 20 minutes. The fraction of initial sample remaining undecayed after 80 minutes is:

allDrafts.stem: A particle starts from rest with uniform acceleration and covers a distance of 100 m in first 10 seconds. The distance covered by it in the next 10 seconds is (in meters):
allDrafts.solution: Distance in first 10 s: S₁₀ = (1/2) a (10)² = 50a = 100 m => a = 2 m/s². Distance in first 20 s: S₂₀ = (1/2) a (20)² = 200a = 200 * 2 = 400 m. Distance in next 10 s: ΔS = S₂₀ - S₁₀ = 400 - 100 = 300 meters.

allDrafts.stem: A parallel plate capacitor of capacitance 10 μF is charged to 100 V and disconnected from the battery. When a dielectric slab of dielectric constant K = 5 is inserted to fill the space between plates completely, the new potential difference across the capacitor in volts is:
allDrafts.solution: Charge Q = C V = 10 μF * 100 V = 1000 μC remains constant when disconnected. New capacitance C' = K C = 5 * 10 μF = 50 μF. New potential difference V' = Q / C' = 1000 μC / 50 μF = 20 V.

allDrafts.stem: In a meter bridge experiment, the balance point is obtained at 40 cm from the zero end when a known resistance of 6 Ω is connected in the right gap. The value of unknown resistance in the left gap in ohms is (give answer as integer / float):
allDrafts.solution: Meter bridge balance condition: R / S = l / (100 - l). Here S = 6 Ω, l = 40 cm => R / 6 = 40 / 60 = 2/3 => R = 6 * (2/3) = 4 Ω.

allDrafts.correctAnswer: B < C < O < N
allDrafts.solution: Ionization enthalpy increases across a period: B < C < O < N. Nitrogen has a half-filled stable 2p³ subshell configuration, making its first IE higher than Oxygen (2p⁴). Thus B < C < O < N.

allDrafts.stem: According to Molecular Orbital Theory, which of the following species is paramagnetic and has a bond order of 2?

allDrafts.solution: O₂ has 16 electrons. MO configuration: σ1s² σ*1s² σ2s² σ*2s² σ2pz² (π2px² = π2py²) (π*2px¹ = π*2py¹). Two unpaired electrons in degenerate antibonding π* orbitals make it paramagnetic. Bond order = (10 - 6)/2 = 2.

allDrafts.stem: For a reaction to be spontaneous at all temperatures, the required thermodynamic conditions are:
allDrafts.correctAnswer: ΔH < 0 and ΔS > 0
allDrafts.solution: Gibbs free energy change: ΔG = ΔH - TΔS. If ΔH < 0 (exothermic) and ΔS > 0 (entropy increase), ΔG is negative at all temperatures T > 0 K, ensuring spontaneity.

allDrafts.stem: If α and β are the roots of equation x² - 6x + c = 0 such that 3α + 2β = 20, then the value of c is:
allDrafts.solution: Sum of roots: α + β = 6 => 2α + 2β = 12. Given 3α + 2β = 20. Subtracting equations: α = 20 - 12 = 8. Then β = 6 - 8 = -2. Product of roots: c = α * β = 8 * (-2) = -16.
